steps.note: Create a reverse auction in the single-stage flow.
Provide the required event title.
a priced single-stage event needs its type set before a template (the screen opens as RFP)
Apply a pricing template before adding line items.
Create the required two-line auction.
Populate the pricing sheet so the event can be scheduled and published.
Commit a live bidding window.
Invite the vendor named in the case.
Publish the auction before bidding.
Verify the auction reached a published project page.
Move to the vendor session while keeping the buyer session open.
Open the live auction's vendor bid sheet.
Establish the closest available initial vendor bid; the catalog applies this value to every price cell.
Verify the initial vendor bid was accepted.
Attempt to open the vendor's bid revision control.
Attempt to change only the second line's price to 45; the line-region label is not catalog-confirmed.
Submit the vendor's revision.
Verify the revised price is visible on the vendor screen.
Return to the buyer's event page to inspect the resulting ranking.
Open the buyer's comparison grid after the vendor revision.
Verify the current reverse-auction ranks follow the lowest amounts.
